brief: A habit tracker as a garden — daily completion waters plants, streaks bloom, neglect wilts

dominant_strengths: Strong central metaphor — pots-as-habits with bloom states maps cleanly to streak data and feels emotionally legible
Sky-to-soil gradient with sun and watering can creates a coherent diorama-like world that reinforces the garden concept
Count badges sit consistently above each pot, giving a scannable streak-at-a-glance reading across the row
dominant_weaknesses: Vast empty sky dominates 70% of the canvas with no secondary content (weather, weekly view, today's tasks), wasting vertical real estate
Bloom states feel under-differentiated — three pots look identical sprouts, breaking the wilt/bloom narrative the brief promises
Generic system sans-serif title clashes with the playful illustrative pots; typography does not commit to the storybook tone
fix_priorities: Populate the sky with meaningful ambient data (today's progress, weather-as-mood, week streak) to justify the composition
Differentiate plant growth stages visually — seedling, sprout, bud, full bloom, wilted — so state reads instantly
Replace the neutral title face with a warmer, hand-drawn or rounded display type aligned to the illustration style
Add subtle motion cues (swaying leaves, falling water droplets) to deliver the watering/bloom feedback loop
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral charm of the garden carries the design, but behavioral feedback is thin and reflective insight (trends, meaning of streaks) is absent.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the metaphor is established, but the wilt/bloom/water states aren't visually distinct enough to make habit health legible.
